ayasofya.ozet_en: Hagia Sophia, officially the Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque, is a mosque and a major cultural and historical site in Istanbul, Turkey. It was formerly a church (360–1453) and a museum (1935–2020). The last of three church buildings to be successively erected on the site by the Eastern Roman Empire, it was completed in AD 537, becoming the world's largest interior space and among the first to employ a fully pendentive dome.

sultanahmet.ozet_en: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque, popularly known as the Blue Mosque, is an Ottoman-era historical imperial mosque located in Istanbul, Turkey. It was constructed between 1609 and 1617 during the rule of Ahmed I. It attracts a large number of tourists and is one of the most iconic and popular monuments of Ottoman architecture.
sultanahmet.yazar: Pedro Szekely from Los Angeles, USA

izmit-saat.ozet_en: The İzmit Clock Tower in İzmit, Turkey is one of many clock towers that were built throughout the Ottoman Empire as a result of the decree which was sent to the provincial governors to commemorate the 25th anniversary of Sultan Abdülhamid II's ascension to the Ottoman throne. It was designed by architect Vedat Tek upon the order of Musa Kazım Bey, the governor of İzmit, and built in 1902. Other sources name the architect of the tower as Mihran Azaryan who was an Armenian-Ottoman of Izmit origin.

ankara-anitkabir.ozet_en: Anıtkabir is a complex located in the Çankaya district of Ankara that contains the mausoleum of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. Designed by Emin Onat and Orhan Arda, construction of Anıtkabir began in 1944 and was completed in 1953. In addition to the mausoleum building and various other structures and monuments, it consists of a wooded area known as the Peace Park.

ankara-kale.ozet_en: Ankara Castle is a historic fortification in the city of Ankara, Turkey, constructed in or after the 7th century. The earliest fortification on the site was constructed in the 8th century BC by the Phrygians and rebuilt in 278 BC by the Galatians. The castle was rebuilt or renovated under the Roman, Byzantine, Seljuk, and Ottoman Empires.

ankara-augustus.ozet_en: The Temple of Augustus and Rome is an augusteum located in the Altındağ district of Ankara. It is thought to have been built around 25–20 BC. Besides being one of the most important Roman-period ruins in the city, it is also known for the Monumentum Ancyranum.

karaman-kale.ozet_en: Karaman Castle is a partly ruined castle in the city of Karaman, central Turkey.

karaman-yunus.ozet_en: Yunus Emre, also known as Derviş Yûnus, was a Turkish folk poet and Sufi who greatly influenced Turkish culture. The UNESCO General Conference unanimously passed a resolution declaring 1991, the 750th anniversary of the poet's birth, International Yunus Emre Year.

balik-ekmek.ozet_en: Balık ekmek is a common street food item in Turkish cuisine. It is a sandwich of a filet of fried or grilled fish, served along with various vegetables, inside a bun of Turkish bread. It is typically served on the Eminönü square straight from the boat on which it is prepared.

baklava.ozet_en: Baklava is a layered pastry dessert made of filo pastry, filled with chopped nuts, and sweetened with either syrup or honey.

pismaniye.ozet_en: Pişmaniye is a Turkish confection made by blending flour roasted in butter into pulled sugar and then forming it into fine strands. It is sometimes garnished with ground pistachio nuts. Although it is sometimes compared to cotton candy, both the ingredients and method of preparation are significantly different.

galata.ozet_en: Galata Tower is a landmark of Istanbul's Beyoğlu district, built as a watchtower within the walls of the Genoese colony of Pera, established in 1267 north of the Golden Horn. Over the centuries it has served several purposes, and since 2020 it has been an exhibition venue and museum. It remains one of the best-known symbols of the city skyline.

ankara-muze.ozet_en: The Museum of Anatolian Civilizations stands on the south side of Ankara Castle and occupies the old Ottoman Mahmut Paşa bazaar storage building and the Kurşunlu Han. Atatürk wished for a Hittite museum, and after restoration (1938–1968) it opened to the public as the Ankara Archaeological Museum. It is one of Turkey's foremost archaeological museums.

coban.ozet_en: The Çoban Mustafa Pasha Complex is an Ottoman külliye in the centre of Gebze, Kocaeli, dating from the 16th century and attributed, though not with certainty, to the architect Sinan. The vizier Çoban Mustafa Pasha, whose mausoleum is in the complex, had it built and it was completed in 1522. He died in 1529 on the way to the Siege of Vienna.

hannibal.ozet_en: Ancient Libyssa lay on the southern shore of the Gulf of İzmit, near today's Gebze. It is chiefly known as the place where the Carthaginian general Hannibal died and where ancient tradition placed his tomb. The memorial in Gebze commemorates this.

simit.ozet_en: Simit is a circular bread encrusted with sesame seeds, found across the cuisines of the former Ottoman Empire, especially in Turkey. It is sold by street vendors and bakeries, for example in Istanbul. In İzmir it is called gevrek, and Ankara's simit are smaller and crisper.

mevlana.ozet_en: The Mevlâna Museum in Konya began as the dervish lodge of the Mevlevi order, better known as the whirling dervishes. It houses the mausoleum of the Sufi mystic Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Rumi (Mevlâna). It is among the most visited sites in Turkey.

alaeddin.ozet_en: The Alâeddin Mosque is the principal monument on Alaaddin Hill in the centre of Konya, and was the main prayer hall of the Seljuk Sultans of Rum. Its courtyard holds the tombs of several sultans. Built in stages between the mid-12th and mid-13th centuries, it is the largest surviving Seljuk mosque in Konya.

ince-minare.ozet_en: İnce Minareli Medrese ('Slender Minaret Madrasa') is a 13th-century madrasa in Konya, an exemplar of Anatolian Seljuk architecture. It is noted for its ornate entrance and domed courtyard, and for its brick minaret, partly destroyed in 1901. It now houses the Museum of Stone and Wood Art.

etli-ekmek.ozet_en: Etli ekmek ('bread with meat') is a traditional dish that originated in Konya. It is a flatbread topped with minced lamb or beef and finely chopped onions, tomatoes and peppers, baked in a stone oven. It is popular across central Turkey and is found in bakeries and specialist restaurants.

ankara-tava.ozet_en: Ankara tava is a dish of the old Ankara cuisine, a meat-and-vegetable rice or vermicelli dish baked in the oven in the meat's own juices. It is one of the best-known local dishes outside Ankara. It is traditionally eaten at weddings, funerals and outings, with cacık, pickles, salad or hoşaf.
